newsitem.title: JAPAN: CSK says cancels plan to buy Bandai shares.
newsitem.headline: CSK says cancels plan to buy Bandai shares.

text.p: CSK Corp said on Thursday that it had cancelled a plan to buy shares in Bandai Co Ltd.
The company also said the failed merger of Sega Enterprises Ltd and Bandai would not have a negative impact on its group earnings for 1997/98.
CSK holds a 20 percent stake in Sega.
CSK also said it expects its parent sales to top 100 billion yen in 1997/98, hitting a record high for the second consecutive year.

Sega, maker of the Saturn 32-bit video-game player, and Bandai, known for its Power Rangers series and virtual pet toy "Tamagotchi", said in January that they would merge to create a global entertainment giant rivalling Walt Disney Co.
CSK chairman Isao Ohkawa was to take the position of chairman of the merged company.
Bandai called off the merger on Tuesday, just one day before the two companies were due to sign a merger pact, saying it was unclear that the merger would yield the synergies originally anticipated.
Bandai's management had been shaken by strong opposition to the merger from mid-level managers who feared a clash in the two companies' corporate cultures and changes in working conditions.
